test_title: PYST 17: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 15 Oct, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The questions in part B looks __difficult__ than the questions in part A.
solution:
The correct answer is: more difficult.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence uses** comparative form** to compare the difficulty levels of questions in part A and part B.
 
• The word **"difficult"** should be made comparative by using **"more"** before it, as "difficult" is a longer adjective.
 
• Instead of using incorrect forms like **"difficultier"** or **"difficulty"**, the correct form is **"more difficult"**.

Correct sentence: *The questions in part B look **more difficult** than the questions in part A*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Adjectives:**

 
 
• **Structure:** Adjective + er (for short adjectives) or more + Adjective (for longer adjectives).
 
• **Example:** This book is **thicker** than that one. / This task is **more complex** than the previous one.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare differences between the two objects they modify (larger, smaller, faster, higher).
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• **Structure: **Adjective + est (for short adjectives) or most + Adjective (for longer adjectives).
 
• **Example: **This is the **tallest** building in the city. / She is the **most talented** artist in the group.
 
• **Usage: **Used to describe an object that is at the upper or lower limit of a quality (the tallest, the smallest, the fastest, the highest).
